'''Thornton Carle Fry''' (7 January 1892, [[Findlay, Ohio]] – 1 January 1991) was an applied mathematician, known for his two widely-used textbooks, ''Probability and its engineering uses'' (1928)<ref>{{cite journal|title=Review of ''Probability and its Engineering Uses'' by T. C. Fry|author=Struik, D. J.|authorlink=Dirk Jan Struik|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.|volume=36|year=1930|pages=19–21|doi=10.1090/S0002-9904-1930-04858-2|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Fry |first1=Thornton |title=Probability and its Engineering Uses |date=1928 |publisher=D. Van Nostrand Company, Inc. |url=https://archive.org/details/probability_and_its_engineering_uses_1928}}</ref> and ''Elementary differential equations'' (1929).<ref>{{cite journal|title=Review of ''Elementary Differential Equations'' by Thornton C. Fry|author=Longley, W. R.|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.|year=1930|volume=36|issue=3|pages=173–174|doi=10.1090/S0002-9904-1930-04918-6|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Fry |first1=Thornton |title=Elementary Differential Equations |date=1929 |publisher=D. Van Nostrand Company, Inc. |url=https://archive.org/details/elementary_differential_equations_1929}}</ref>

== Career ==
Thornton C. Fry received his bachelor's degree from [[Findlay College]] in 1912 and then pursued graduate study in Wisconsin in mathematics, physics, and astronomy. He received his M.A. in 1913<ref>{{cite book|author=Fry, Thornton Carle|title=A contact transformation|publisher=University of Wisconsin-Madison|year=1913|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=lqpbAAAAMAAJ}}</ref> and his Ph.D. in 1920 in [[applied mathematics]] from the [[University of Wisconsin-Madison]] with thesis under the supervision of [[Charles S. Slichter]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=7947}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|author=Fry, Thornton Carle|title=The Application of Modern Theories of Integration to the Solution of Differential Equations|publisher=University of Wisconsin-Madison|year=1921|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=NqhNAAAAMAAJ}}</ref>

Fry was employed as an industrial mathematician by [[Western Electric Company]] from 1916 to 1924 and then by [[Bell Telephone Laboratories]] (Bell Labs), which was half-owned by Western Electric. He headed a corporate division for industrial applications of mathematics and statistics and was involved in [[research and development]] for the U.S. federal government in both world wars.

After retiring (due to reaching the mandatory retirement age) from Bell Labs in 1956, he was hired by [[William Norris (CEO)|William Norris]] as a Senior Consultant for the [[UNIVAC]] division of [[Sperry Corporation#Sperry Rand|Sperry Rand]]. He would subsequently be appointed as Vice-President head of the UNIVAC Division over Norris in April 1957.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Norberg |first1=Arthur L. |title=Computers and commerce: a study of technology and management at Eckert-Mauchly Computer Company, Engineering Research Associates, and Remington Rand, 1946-1957 |date=2005 |publisher=MIT Press |location=Cambridge, Mass |isbn=978-0-262-14090-4 |pages=262, 265–266, 273 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-f7NIGeIU2EC&pg=PA273 |access-date=23 October 2023 |language=en}}</ref> After retiring from Sperry-Rand in 1961 he worked as a consultant with Boeing Scientific Research Labs and also, during the 1960s, with [[Walter Orr Roberts]], director of the [[National Center for Atmospheric Research]].<ref>{{cite journal|journal=Bulletin of the American Astronomical Society|title=Obituary. Thornton Carl (''sic'') Fry, 1892–1991s|author=Firor, John|authorlink=John W. Firor|author2=Trimble, Virginia|authorlink2=Virginia Louise Trimble|year=1997|volume=29|issue=4|pages=1470–1471|bibcode=1997BAAS...29.1470F}} This obituary and several other sources have the name "Thornton Carl Fry" instead of the correct "Thornton Carle Fry".</ref>

In 1924 Fry was an Invited Speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Toronto.<ref>{{cite book|author=Fry, T. C.|title=Proc. Intern. Mathematical Congress held in Toronto, 1924|volume=2|pages=407–428|chapter=The use of the integraph in the practical solution of differential equations by Picard's method of successive approximations}} (See [[integraph]].)</ref> In 1982 the [[Mathematical Association of America]] (MAA) gave him the MAA's distinguished service award.<ref>{{cite journal|journal=American Mathematical Monthly|author=Price, G. Baley|authorlink=Griffith Baley Price|title=Award for distinguished Service to Dr. Thornton Carl (''sic'') Fry|date=1982 |volume=89|issue=2|pages=81–83|doi=10.1080/00029890.1982.11995388}}</ref>
